questions.q: A candidate model has ROC AUC 0.72 and clears the 0.70 floor, but the champion scores 0.744 on the same data. With max_drop set to 0.01, what does the gate do?
options: Blocks it, because it is worse than the champion by more than 0.01
Passes it, because it is above the floor
Passes it, because average precision is not checked
Retrains the champion automatically
questions.explain: The gate checks floors and also compares with the champion. 0.72 is 0.024 below 0.744, which exceeds the 0.01 allowed drop, so the candidate is blocked.

questions.q: Why does the capstone separate register from promote?
options: MLflow cannot do both in one call
Promotion is what trains the model
It reduces the size of the mlruns folder
So a new version can be contract-tested before it becomes the version anyone serves
questions.explain: Registering only creates a version. The champion alias moves in promote, which runs after the contract test, so a bad version never becomes the served model.

questions.q: Why must the candidate and the champion be evaluated on the same data inside the gate?
options: It makes evaluation faster
MLflow requires identical data for registration
Otherwise the comparison mixes model quality with differences in the data
It guarantees the candidate passes
questions.explain: If the two models were scored on different datasets, a difference in AUC could just reflect an easier or harder sample. A fair comparison uses one evaluation set.

questions.q: In the drift check, week 4 raised an alarm with days_idle at PSI 0.867 while the other features stayed at 0.013 or lower. What does the alarm mean?
options: The model's accuracy has definitely collapsed
One input's distribution moved a lot, which is a reason to investigate, not proof of harm
All eight features drifted
The model must be retrained immediately
questions.explain: PSI measures input change, and lesson 18 showed input drift alone often does not hurt accuracy. The retrain decision function answers 'investigate' unless AUC also breaches its floor.

questions.q: What does the contract test check?
options: Only that the model file exists
That the model's accuracy is above 90 percent
That the training data has no missing values
That the running API keeps its promises: valid input works, bad input gets a 422, the response shape is right
questions.explain: A contract test exercises the running API the way a caller would, checking the promises made about its inputs, outputs and errors.
